Alf Orton was third, but with the scoring 5, 3, 1, it will be seen that it was almost essential to have first places in order to keep ahead. The 440 yards found a similar result in that Baker scored a win for the home side; and we filled the minor places with N.C.

Bishop, 2 min. 10 secs. 1 mile: Herbert, 4 min. 52 secs., 3rd, Short Relay (4 x half a lap), 1st, Epsom; 2nd, Bels. (Grimshaw, Simmons, Walden and Broadbent); 3rd, Bel, Juniors (Marshall, Baker, Mullen, Sexton).
These included Pat Sapcote and Jack Baker. The unusual distance of the race got the team selectors guessing with the result that two of our “ B ” team men finished before the second “ A ” team man.

Those to have finished the distance inside 9 hours and excluding the performances just quoted are Bellchamber (twice), Miles, Rathbone, Bentley, Martin (R.) (4 times), Bidgood (3 times), Rickards (twice), Urry (twice), Sutton (twice), Baker and Stirling Wakeley.
When the field had settled down, Jim Masters was running 3rd with Baker of the local club who eventually beat him and our scoring six were in the first thirty.
The R.A.M.C. were unable to compete in every event, but in winning the 880 yards their runner Baker scored a fine win in 1m.58.5s. closely followed by B.

After 2½ miles Howard(Watford) led the field from Lindsell (Portsmouth) and Baker(Walton). Ken Miller was now 29th, John Thresher 50th, Derek Crookes 92nd and Jim Radford 107th; Trevor Hart being forced to drop back a considerable way with trouble from a shoulder ailment.

The race was won by Roath of Walton(56:11)from Goode of Epsom with Baker of Horsham 3rd. Walker(59:28 9th),Moore(60.49,13th), and E.Bishop (62:12,16th) completed our scoring trio and they managed to snatch 3rd place from S.L.H. in what was a desperately close finish.
Dave King came through well followed by Pat Duncan. Without Farley, Baker, Cameron or Picton it was left to John Keown to bring the team in fourth.

Hall, Bonser, Mathews, Baker, etc. - a band of stalwarts who with Lionel have travelled many expensive miles this season to take part in some gruelling events and have made sure that Belgrave has been represented far and near.

Others forced to withdraw were Hilton, Baker, Paget, Laws and Fairfield. The organisation was as excellent as usual and Gordon Biscoe now becomes our longest serving race secretary for this promotion with six consecutive efforts, one ahead of Arthur Whitehead who initiated the event 21 years ago.

In hot-blooded Anglo-Saxon his rivals are decried and with arms waving and eyes glittering he will spit out threats to that "*****bald headed old ***** Baker" and anyone else who dares to suggest that they will beat him next time out.
To go to the head of the field and win the race and to be acclaimed with the names of Whitlock, Baker, Thompson, Pamich, Middleton is something extra.
